subject.title: [Feature Request] SKILL.md Instruction Isolation from Agent Context

question: What trusted/untrusted boundary should OpenClaw enforce for model-visible SKILL.md content?
rationale: The fix defines a public security boundary across prompts, memory, tools, sandbox behavior, skill metadata, and compatibility defaults, so automation cannot safely choose the policy shape.

options.title: Approve phased core boundary
options.body: Define the skill trust contract first, then split implementation into schema/diagnostics, prompt and read handling, execution enforcement, memory boundaries, tests, and docs.

options.title: Start with metadata only
options.body: Add inspectable capability metadata without enforcement, reducing compatibility risk but leaving instruction isolation unresolved for now.

options.title: Treat as external policy only
options.body: Leave core behavior unchanged and rely on governance/scanner plugins, accepting that the built-in model-facing SKILL.md path remains a soft prompt boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve phased core boundary
recommendation.body: Define the skill trust contract first, then split implementation into schema/diagnostics, prompt and read handling, execution enforcement, memory boundaries, tests, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The live discussion and adjacent history point to steipete as the strongest available security/product routing candidate for this boundary decision.
